environment.description: Same ASP.NET Core 8 application packaged as a container image and deployed as an AWS Lambda function with a Function URL. The Function URL is configured with AuthType=AWS_IAM. The Lambda execution role has a resource-based policy that only grants lambda:InvokeFunctionUrl to principals within the same AWS Organization (condition: aws:PrincipalOrgID). The function runs in a dedicated Lambda execution environment where /tmp is an ephemeral 512MB storage isolated per invocation sandbox. There is no SigV4 signing proxy or API Gateway in front - callers must present valid SigV4 credentials directly to the Function URL endpoint. CloudTrail logs all invocation attempts including 403 responses from unsigned requests.

config.deployment: AWS Lambda with Function URL (AuthType: AWS_IAM)
config.network: Function URL endpoint, no VPC attachment
config.auth: AWS_IAM auth on Function URL, resource policy restricts to aws:PrincipalOrgID=o-abc123def4
config.filesystem: /tmp is ephemeral per-sandbox, 512MB, isolated per concurrent invocation
config.iam_policy: Resource-based policy: Effect=Allow, Principal=*, Action=lambda:InvokeFunctionUrl, Condition={StringEquals: {aws:PrincipalOrgID: o-abc123def4}}
config.monitoring: CloudTrail data events enabled for Lambda
